title: The Tseitin clauses for an AND gate define the gate
statement: For all propositions a, b, t: the conjunction of the three clauses ((not t) or a), ((not t) or b) and (t or (not a) or (not b)) is equivalent to t if and only if (a and b).

formal.statement: (assert (= (and (or (not t) a) (or (not t) b) (or t (not a) (not b))) (= t (and a b))))

evidence.supports: For all propositions a, b, t: the conjunction of the three clauses ((not t) or a), ((not t) or b) and (t or (not a) or (not b)) is equivalent to t if and only if (a and b).

notes:
The correctness core of our own CNF encoder, stated as a proposition and checked. Not merely equisatisfiable: the clause set is EQUIVALENT to the gate definition, which is the stronger property that makes the encoding model-preserving and so makes model lifting through Tseitin sound. What remains unstated -- and is the real theorem -- is that the recursive Tseitin transformation of an ARBITRARY formula is equisatisfiable with it. That quantifies over formulas; we have no object for a formula, so this single gate is the largest instance we can pin.

On the axiom footprint: it names the trust base of the SMT ROUTE that established this fact -- the axeyum-ir Boolean evaluator, and the two-valued semantics of the SMT-LIB Bool sort that makes exhaustive truth-table enumeration a proof. It is deliberately NOT empty and deliberately NOT a Lean axiom list. Nothing here went through axeyum's Lean kernel. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_axiom_inventory`: the `logic` prelude reports axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0, and its declarations are exactly True, False, And, Or, Iff, Not (as `a -> False`), Eq and Exists -- an intuitionistic core with no `Classical.em`, no `propext` and no `Quot.sound`. Zero trusted declarations there means the kernel assumes nothing, not that it can prove everything.
